selection: Twentieth-century Brazilian modernist literary fiction by a major woman writer, shifting the rotation from R. K. Narayan’s South Asian comic fiction while broadening the collection’s Latin American representation beyond its existing male authors.

sources.use: The Instituto Moreira Salles chronology identifies Lispector as a major Brazilian writer and documents her 1943 debut, The Passion According to G.H. in 1964 and The Hour of the Star in 1977.

The author archive’s book-by-book catalogue supplies the original publication sequence and classifications for the seven selected novels and novella, and distinguishes other genres and posthumous books.

Lispector’s English-language publisher confirms her 1920–1977 lifespan, the 1943 Rio publication of Near to the Wild Heart, the 1973 date of Água Viva, later English translations and the posthumous status of A Breath of Life.

A translated 1976 interview with Lispector distinguishes writing from publication: The Chandelier was published in 1946, The Passion According to G.H. was written in 1963 and published in 1964, and An Apprenticeship appeared in 1969.

verifiedScope.proxy: Lifetime original-Portuguese novel and novella book-publication span from Lispector’s debut novel to the last book she published, used as a publishing proxy rather than a complete bibliography or claim of uninterrupted work.
workDates: 1969 — An Apprenticeship or the Book of Pleasures
verifiedScope.dateDistinctions: Markers use original Brazilian Portuguese book-publication years, not composition, earlier periodical appearances, revised editions or later translations. The Chandelier was completed before its 1946 publication; The Passion According to G.H. was written in 1963 and published in 1964; and Água Viva was transformed from the unpublished manuscript Screaming Object before its 1973 book. None of the selected markers is a translation or posthumous first release. The posthumous A Breath of Life (1978), assembled by Olga Borelli from Lispector’s fragments, does not extend the lifetime bar; short stories, children’s books, crônicas, journalism and translation work are excluded from the scoped span.
verifiedScope.chartRange: Lispector’s 1920–1977 lifespan falls within the collection-derived chart domain, so no chart-range change was required.
verifiedScope.influence: No claim of influence is inferred from chronological overlap.
